title: Pricing by hours per project for Landscaping
audience: Owners and supervisors of landscaping crews who write quotes for planting, paving and planned works, and need a price that covers cost and earns a margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures
Estimate project hours for a landscaping job, including set-up, travel and checking time
Build a landscaping quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit
instruction.body: Landscaping is labour-heavy, and its hours change with the site: soil, access, the number of plants, the handling of materials and the clean-up. Hours make those differences visible. A price per square metre from a cost guide is a market check, not a costing method, because it does not show how many hours your crew needs on your site.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the year's total cost of running the crew and the business by the chargeable hours. Include wages with on-costs such as leave and superannuation (business.gov.au, updated 1 October 2026), plant running costs (the Melbourne cost guide lists a bobcat or mini excavator with operator at $81 to $145 per hour, verified 1 November 2026), the trailer and vehicle, tools, insurance, administration and premises. Use chargeable hours, not paid hours. Confirm the award or agreement for each worker, because pay rates are not stated in this lesson.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours
instruction.body: Break the job into site set-up, preparation, planting or paving, materials handling, clean-up, travel and checking. Estimate each task as a range from your own project log. Add set-up, pack-down and travel as named lines. Add a set allowance for delays such as delivery problems, weather and access. Xero suggests 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work (Xero Australia, 3 September 2026); size your own allowance from records. Back-cost past projects against the quote before you rely on standard times (Carters Trade Leader, 1 October 2025; New Zealand source, method only).

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price
instruction.body: Multiply crew hours by your cost per productive hour, add plant hire and materials on their own lines at cost plus your stated policy, add the margin for risk (for example, a tight deadline or a difficult site), and apply the minimum charge. Use the cost guide as a cross-check only. It lists a new garden bed at $45, $90 and $160 per m², and paving at $54, $90 and $145 per m² (What's the Damage, verified 1 November 2026). The page does not say what those rates include, so the check is rough.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: A quote states the scope and boundary, the hours or price basis, exclusions (for example, retaining structures, trees, or services not in the scope), what the client provides (access, approvals and checks on services in the ground), GST status and validity. Significant design changes and major landscaping may need a strata general meeting resolution (Clean Group, 9 March 2026), so state that approval is the client's responsibility. Re-quote when the scope changes, and record the change in writing (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026).

instruction.heading: Review your estimates
instruction.body: Compare estimated and actual hours for at least the first ten projects of each type. If the variance is above your threshold, change the standard time, the margin or the scope rules. Review prices about every three months (Business Victoria, undated).

procedure: Gather the year's total business costs and the productive hours achieved in the same period.
Divide total costs by productive hours to get the cost per productive hour.
Break each project into tasks and estimate each task time as a range.
Add set-up, pack-down, travel and checking time as named lines.
Multiply crew hours by the cost per productive hour, add plant and materials on their own lines, add the delay allowance, then apply the margin.
Apply the materials policy and the minimum charge.
Write the quote with scope, boundary, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs, GST status and validity.
Record actual hours after each project and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A 20 m² planting bed needs 16 crew-hours on site (two people for eight hours, illustrative), including set-up, planting, mulching and clean-up, plus 1 hour of travel. The owner's cost per productive hour is $60 (illustrative). The target margin on price is 25 per cent (illustrative). Plants and mulch are on a separate materials line.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the labour price with a 25 per cent margin, and how does the cost guide's rough check compare?
workedExamples.reasoning: The crew-hours total 17, so the labour cost is 17 multiplied by $60, which is $1,020. A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is $1,020 divided by 0.75, which is $1,360, before materials. The cost guide's new-bed rate of $90 per m² gives $1,800 for 20 m² (What's the Damage), but that page does not say what the rate includes, so the gap does not show either figure is wrong. The owner checks the planting hours first, because an error in hours changes the price more than a small change in rate. Materials go on their own line, so the final price is not complete until they are priced.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each project, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for bed areas

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the labour wage alone
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, plant and vehicle costs, consumables, insurance and administration in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Counting paid hours as productive hours
commonErrors.prevention: Use chargeable hours only when calculating the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out travel, set-up and checking time
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every estimate.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no exclusions or boundary
commonErrors.prevention: List what is excluded, including retaining structures and services not in the scope, and state the boundary in writing.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimates with actual hours
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual hours after each project and review the variance monthly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies to pricing statements, and misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026). State and territory fair trading rules also apply and differ, so check the rules for your state.
Pay rates and on-costs may be set by an award or enterprise agreement. Check which applies to each worker before using any wage figure. This lesson does not state pay rates.

In Victoria, the scope boundary can decide whether a registered practitioner is needed: over $10,000 for domestic building work (Victorian Building Authority, undated). Price any work that may be domestic building work only after checking that boundary. NSW structural landscaping over $5,000 including GST needs a licence (NSW Government, 23 June 2026).

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, boundary, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs, GST status and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten projects of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision, a materials line and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, boundary, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Project time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Hours make the work visible, so start every landscaping quote from hours.
Cost per productive hour uses chargeable time, not paid time.
Plant, materials, travel and checking time are named lines, not hidden extras.
Compare estimates with actual hours, and change the method when they diverge.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker and nothing else from the accounts or the rent
The price the client pays, plus the deposit, the late fee and the crew bonus paid
The average hourly rate of competitors in the local area and their fees for the whole year
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, equipment, consumables, insurance and administration, divided by chargeable hours

knowledgeChecks.question: A planting project is estimated at 5 crew-hours and takes 8. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, since the client has already paid and the crew has finished
Reduce paid hours for the crew on the next job and skip the morning break
Raise the price for this client's next job only and no one else is charged more

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a landscaping quote need an exclusions list and a stated boundary?
options: To hide the margin from the client and to keep the rates a secret from the crew
To make the quote longer and to fill up the page with more text and words for the client
To show what the price covers, so scope changes can be priced and disputes are reduced
To lower the client's expectations and to make the job seem much smaller than it is

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

New Zealand publisher; general method only. Supports: compare quoted and actual labour.

What's the Damage, 'Landscaping cost Melbourne', https://whatsthedamage.com.au/landscaping-cost-melbourne/, verified 1 November 2026. Cost guide; not a regulator. Supports: bobcat with operator $81 to $145 per hour; new garden bed and paving per m² ranges. GST treatment not stated.
Clean Group, strata gardening guide, https://www.clean-group.com.au/?p=195299, updated 9 March 2026. Vendor source. Supports: major landscaping may need a general meeting resolution.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Estimates, quotes and deposits', https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/estimates-quotes-and-deposits, last updated 4 September 2026. Western Australia only. Supports: record changes to quotes; total including GST.

Business Victoria, 'Develop a pricing strategy', https://business.vic.gov.au/business-information/finance/pricing-for-profit/develop-a-pricing-strategy, no date shown. Supports: include total overheads and sales costs when checking a price; review about every three months.

Victorian Building Authority, 'Landscaping', https://www.vba.vic.gov.au/consumers/home-renovation-essentials/landscaping, no date shown. Supports: registered practitioner threshold for domestic building work over $10,000.
